previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with confusion and dehydration following recent breast reduction surgery and a prior UTI. She was found to have healthcare-associated pneumonia, an NSTEMI, and acute kidney injury. Her troponin peaked at 3.09 and trended down without chest pain. She was treated with IV antibiotics, later transitioned to oral levofloxacin, and managed for NSTEMI with aspirin and pravastatin. Her immunosuppressants were adjusted due to transaminitis and renal concerns. She developed antibiotic-associated diarrhea, which was C. diff negative. Her mental status improved, and she was discharged home with stable vital signs, improved oxygenation, and plans for outpatient follow-up with cardiology, transplant nephrology, and primary care.

Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted for neck and shoulder tightness, along with 
nausea and epigastric pain.  Markers of cardiac damage were 
slightly elevated, which is not uncommon with renal disease.

showed a fixed defect in your heart muscle that would not 
benefit from intervention. An echo showed that your heart 
function was low normal.  Your symptoms resolved and you were 
stable for discharge.

While you were here, renal transplant physicians were consulted 
and monitored your kidney function.  

We increased the dose of your tacrolimus and sirolimus due to a 
low levels. We have stopped your amlodipine due to low blood 
pressure while inptaient. We have started atorvastatin to 
replace your pravastatin to prevent coronary plaque. We have 
also started plavix, an antiplatelet medication to prevent blood 
clots in your coronary artries. Please take all your remaining

EXAMINATION:  RENAL TRANSPLANT U.S.

INDICATION:  ___ with elevated Cr with transplant kidney

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale as well as color and spectral Doppler ultrasound images
of the renal transplant were obtained.

COMPARISON:  Ultrasound dated ___

FINDINGS: 

The right iliac fossa transplant renal morphology is normal.  Specifically,
the cortex is of normal thickness and echogenicity, pyramids are normal, there
is no urothelial thickening, and renal sinus fat is normal.  There is no
hydronephrosis and no perinephric fluid collection. Mild pelviectasis within
the upper pole resolved upon emptying of the bladder.

The resistive index of intrarenal arteries ranges from 0.68 to 0.73, slightly
elevated. The main renal artery shows a normal waveform, with prompt systolic
upstroke and continuous antegrade diastolic flow, with peak systolic velocity
of 57 cm/sec. Vascularity is symmetric throughout transplant. The transplant
renal vein is patent and shows normal waveform.

IMPRESSION: 

Mildly elevated resistive indices up to 0.73, previously up to 0.66. No
hydronephrosis or perinephric fluid collection. Patent renal vasculature with
normal waveforms.
